## What changed

Publishing. The fork reaches npm as **`@plebeiantech/lat.md`** so that
[mise](https://mise.jdx.dev/) can install it, which a tarball URL cannot do —
`mise use -g npm:lat.md` resolves to *upstream's* build, without any of the
fork's checks.

- Published under a scope the fork owns, making a collision with upstream's
  `lat.md` impossible.
- Authentication is npm **Trusted Publishing** (OIDC) rather than a long-lived
  token. A classic Publish token fails in CI with `EOTP`, because publishing
  under 2FA asks for a one-time password no workflow can supply.
- `--tag latest` at publish time, which npm requires for a prerelease and which
  is the only tag an OIDC credential can ever set.
- `repository.url` repointed at the fork, without which `--provenance` is
  rejected with a 422 naming both URLs.
- A version-free `lat.md-latest.tgz` asset, so the install URL never changes.
  GitHub's `/releases/latest/` redirect resolves the release but not an asset
  name.
